assertions.evidence: "Risk score exactly at threshold", "Well below threshold, any applicant"

assertions.text: Test method body contains no if or switch statements
assertions.evidence: 3 method(s) checked — no if/switch/ternary

assertions.text: Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case.

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: @Description uses text block or is short single-line

assertions.text: Multiple tables each addressing a distinct concern, not one monolithic table
assertions.evidence: Three @TableTest methods: autoApprovesRenewalsWithNoClaims, rejectsApplicationsAboveRiskThreshold, calculatesPremiumByAgeTier

assertions.text: Each table has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules
assertions.evidence: Table 1 mixes decision+premium, requiring both a 'standard' and 'senior' renewal row (age 30 and 70) just to show the bypass overrides both paths

assertions.text: Decision logic and premium calculation are in separate @TableTest methods
assertions.evidence: autoApprovesRenewalsWithNoClaims and rejectsApplicationsAboveRiskThreshold both assert 'status' AND 'premium' together

assertions.text: Test method body does not recompute internal formulas
assertions.evidence: assertEquals(status, result.decision()); assertEquals(premium, result.premium(), 0.001);

assertions.text: @Description explains business context, not internal formulas
assertions.evidence: "Risk score is age/10 + claimCount * 15. Applications are rejected once the score exceeds 75."

assertions.text: Approval decision table covers rejection boundary with 4 vs 5 claims across ages
assertions.evidence: Boundary rows use age9/claims5 (score 75) vs age10/claims5 (score 76), not 4-vs-5 claims across varying ages

assertions.text: Approved premium table covers boundary effects: the premium jump from 0 to 1 claim (impact of +15 risk score on premium), and the premium difference at age 64 vs 65 (standard vs senior formula).
assertions.evidence: Rows show 106.00 (claims=0) vs 136.00 (claims=1) at age 30, and 142.00 (age 64) vs 273.50 (age 65) in calculatesPremiumByAgeTier.

assertions.text: The build file (build.gradle) includes org.tabletest:tabletest-junit as a test dependency

assertions.text: Cell values make the rule falsifiable, not merely distinguishable.

assertions.text: A reader can state the rule from the table alone, without the test method body.
assertions.evidence: Description states: 'Risk score is age/10 + claimCount * 15. Applications are rejected once the score exceeds 75.' and 'charged 100 + riskScore * 2.0 below age 65, and 200 + riskScore * 3.5 from age 65 onward.'

assertions.text: Each @DisplayName (or method name) states what the code under test does.
assertions.evidence: Method names: autoApprovesRenewalsWithNoClaims, rejectsApplicationsAboveRiskThreshold, calculatesPremiumByAgeTier — active verbs naming the SUT's actions.
